learningGoals: Observe pictures carefully and talk about what they see. 👀
Learn new English words for everyday objects shown in the scenes. 🔤
Form simple, short sentences to describe an image or a situation. 🗣️
Build confidence in expressing thoughts and imagination in English. 🌟
teachingTips: Point to different parts of a picture and ask 'What is this?' or 'Who is that?' to encourage your child to speak. 👆
Help them form complete sentences. If they point and say 'bird', smile and reply 'Yes, the bird is flying!' 🦅
Be patient and let them use their wonderful imagination to create a small story behind the picture. 💭
Praise their efforts enthusiastically, even if they use a mix of their mother tongue and English at first. 👏

funActivities.title: I Spy With My Little Eye 👁️
funActivities.description: Open a page in the book with a busy scene. Say 'I spy something green' or 'I spy a dog'. Let your child find and name the object in English.

funActivities.title: My Beautiful Drawing 🖍️
funActivities.description: Ask your child to draw a simple picture of your family, home, or a park. Then, sit together and encourage them to name the things they drew in English.

funActivities.title: Family Photo Storyteller 📖
funActivities.description: Look at an old family photograph or a magazine picture together. Ask your child simple questions like 'Who is this?' or 'What are we doing?' to practice observation and speaking.
